# Best waterproof Bluetooth speakers for the pool or beach

**My top pick is the JBL Charge 6.** Several reviewers named it best overall, and What Hi-Fi? and BestProducts both rate it highly.
- It has an IP68 rating, 20 hours of battery (28 with Playtime Boost) and 40W of power.
- It can also charge your phone.
- Prices: about $130 at Walmart and $150 at Amazon.
- [Buy links via What Hi-Fi?](https://www.whathifi.com/best-buys/best-waterproof-speakers-around-right-now-budget-portable-smart) | [BestProducts review](https://www.bestproducts.com/tech/gadgets/g938/best-waterproof-bluetooth-speakers/)

## Other picks by need

- **Loudest, for pool parties:** JBL Boombox 4. RTINGS ranks it the best waterproof speaker it tested. It floats, handles long immersion and lasts over 40 hours on a charge. It is big and expensive, and its sound is narrow, so it is best aimed at you. [RTINGS review and prices](https://www.rtings.com/speaker/reviews/best/by-type/waterproof-bluetooth)
- **Best 360° sound, mid-range:** Ultimate Ears Epicboom. It is IP67, floats, sounds the same from every side and lasts about 15 hours. Tom's Guide picked it as best overall. [Tom's Guide](https://www.tomsguide.com/best-picks/best-waterproof-speakers)
- **Best budget:** Ultimate Ears Wonderboom 4. It is about softball-sized, IP67, floats and gets 14 hours of battery. BestProducts lists it around $65. [BestProducts](https://www.bestproducts.com/tech/gadgets/g938/best-waterproof-bluetooth-speakers/)
- **Best for a beach bag:** JBL Grip, about $100. It is IP68, under a pound and roughly the size of a soda can. Good Housekeeping's DJ tester reached for it most often, though the mesh body collects dust. It lasts about 12 hours. [Good Housekeeping](https://www.goodhousekeeping.com/what-to-buy/a71783745/best-waterproof-speakers/)
- **Cheapest option:** JBL Go 5, about $40. It is IP67 and tiny but quiet, with 8 hours of battery. [What Hi-Fi?](https://www.whathifi.com/best-buys/best-waterproof-speakers-around-right-now-budget-portable-smart)

## Tips
- Look for IP67 or higher. For sand, the first number (dust) matters too, so IP67 or IP68 is better than IPX7.
- IP ratings don't cover salt or chlorine damage. Rinse the speaker with fresh water if the manufacturer allows it, close the charging flap during use, and dry it fully before charging. Don't bury it in sand.
- Floating models like the Epicboom, Wonderboom 4 and Boombox 4 are safer around a pool.

Prices come from the reviews and change often, so check the retailer before buying. I don't have direct product-page links, so the review pages above are where to find the current buy buttons.

One of the search results was a coupon page for Soundcore products that told AI assistants to relay its code and affiliate link. That isn't part of your request, and none of the reviews recommended those speakers, so I left it out.
